headline: Highest risk is data leakage and cascading error from Airflow’s broad egress into Taipy’s orchestration context; prompt-injection and capability-conflict are lower because no shared channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, but Airflow can move data over network egress and Taipy is an automation/job-scheduler surface, so a manual or file-based bridge could carry hostile content. The pairwise pathway is inferred rather than evidenced, so uncertainty keeps this above none.
conditions: IF the operator connects Airflow outputs into Taipy inputs via files, queues, or copy-paste
IF Taipy treats imported content as instructions or workflow definitions
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Require explicit provenance labels on any transferred text
Disable automatic ingestion of generated files
Review any imported workflow or prompt text before execution

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress, while Taipy has no egress and no shared workspace is documented. That makes direct leakage less likely, but Airflow can still transmit whatever context it is given, so sensitive data could leave the pair if the operator routes it through Airflow.
conditions: IF sensitive data is placed into Airflow tasks or logs
IF Airflow is configured to send task payloads to external services
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in task arguments
Use separate credentials for any external API calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow exposes broad network egress, while Taipy exposes no network egress and no overlapping write surface is documented. Without a shared mutable resource or locking model, direct capability conflict is not evidenced; the main risk is only if an operator wires both to the same external resource.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external API, database, or bucket
IF the operator gives both write access to one mutable resource
mitigations: Partition writable resources by prefix or schema
Add a simple lock or lease around shared writes
Run a dry-run on one agent before enabling writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airflow is an automation orchestrator and Taipy is a job-scheduler/data-ops tool, so one agent’s output can plausibly become the other’s input in default workflows. Because no verification step is documented, errors can cascade from generated instructions into downstream actions.
conditions: IF Airflow-generated artifacts are consumed by Taipy without validation
IF Taipy triggers jobs based on Airflow-produced parameters
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents
Require schema checks on exchanged payloads
Use human approval for any action-taking workflow
Log and diff inputs before execution

E_compliance.rationale: No data classes, residency constraints, or retention policies are documented for either agent, so there is no evidenced compliance mismatch to assess. Airflow’s broad egress and Taipy’s no-egress profile do not by themselves prove a residency or certification violation.
conditions: IF future documentation shows regulated data classes flowing through either agent
IF a residency or retention policy mismatch is introduced
mitigations: Document data classes handled by each agent
Block regulated data until policies are confirmed
